config.title: Design Real-Time Dashboard

intro.title: Design Real-Time Dashboard
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a real-time dashboard that displays live data updates, such as stock prices or user activity. You will learn how to use Vue's reactive state system to automatically update the UI when data changes. The main technologies involved are Vue components, reactive data properties, and conditional rendering. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to create dynamic, data-driven interfaces in Vue.
intro.usecase: Real-time dashboards are essential in modern applications where live data visualization drives decision-making. Developers implement these patterns in financial trading platforms that display stock price fluctuations, operations centers monitoring server health metrics, and logistics systems tracking delivery vehicles on interactive maps. These dashboards typically combine live data feeds with interactive charts, status indicators, and filtering controls that update without page refreshes. Mastering this pattern enables you to build responsive monitoring tools, analytics interfaces, and live reporting systems that users rely on for up-to-the-second information.

objectives: Construct a Vue component with reactive data properties for dashboard metrics
Initialize and configure real-time data updates using lifecycle hooks
Implement computed properties to transform and format raw dashboard data
Bind dynamic CSS classes to visualize metric thresholds and status changes
Control the rendering of dashboard sections with conditional directives
Integrate event handlers to manage user interactions with dashboard controls
Manipulate component state in response to simulated real-time data streams
Apply Vue's reactivity system to automatically update the dashboard UI

steps.title: Import Vue and reactive from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the reactive function from the 'vue' package to set up the foundation for your dashboard component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both Vue and reactive from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to create a Vue component with reactive state.
successCriteria: Vue and reactive are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Vue and reactive from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Vue and reactive from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create Dashboard component
steps.instruction: Define and export a Vue component named Dashboard with a setup function that returns an empty template.
steps.hint: Create a component using Vue's defineComponent or a simple setup function. Export it as the default export.
steps.seedCode:
import { reactive } from 'vue'

// Define and export the Dashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Dashboard component is created and exported, ready to be the main component of the dashboard.
successCriteria: Dashboard component is defined with a setup function and exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Dashboard component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Dashboard and has a setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Dashboard component wasn't created correctly. Check the component name and structure.

steps.title: Initialize reactive dashboard data
steps.instruction: Inside your Dashboard component, create a reactive object called 'dashboardData' with initial values for userCount, revenue, and activeUsers.
steps.hint: Use the reactive() function you imported to create a reactive object with three properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a reactive object with three properties that will hold your dashboard metrics.
successCriteria: A reactive object named 'dashboardData' exists with properties userCount, revenue, and activeUsers set to initial values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're creating a reactive object with all three required properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a reactive object with the three properties: userCount, revenue, and activeUsers.

steps.title: Define updateMetrics handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named updateMetrics that will simulate updating the dashboard metrics with random values.
steps.hint: Create a function that will later be used to update the reactive data. You can define it as a regular function or arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The updateMetrics function is defined inside the setup function, ready to be used for updating dashboard metrics.
successCriteria: The updateMetrics function is properly defined within the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the updateMetrics function is defined inside the setup function. Check that you've spelled the function name correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateMetrics function isn't defined correctly. Make sure to create a function named updateMetrics inside the setup function.

steps.title: Set up template structure
steps.instruction: Inside the Dashboard component's setup function, return a template object containing a container div with a header element inside it.
steps.hint: The template should be returned from the setup function. Use a div with a header element inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component now returns a basic template structure with a container div and header.
successCriteria: The setup function returns a template object containing a div with a header element inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a template object from the setup function with a div containing a header.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Remember to return a template object from setup() with a div and header.

steps.title: Add metrics display section
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a <div> element with the class 'metrics' to serve as a container for your metric cards.
steps.hint: Place the <div class="metrics"> inside the template section where you want the metrics to appear.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: adding a container div
steps.expectedOutcome: A div with class 'metrics' is added to the template, ready to hold metric cards.
successCriteria: The template contains a <div class="metrics"> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a <div> with class="metrics" inside the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metrics container wasn't added correctly. Add a <div class="metrics"> element to the template.

steps.title: Create user count metric card
steps.instruction: Inside the template structure, add a div element that displays the userCount value from your reactive dashboard data.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output reactive data values in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying reactive data in Vue template
Active users: {{ userCount }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a metric card that displays the current user count value from the reactive state.
successCriteria: A div element is added inside the metrics-section that displays the userCount value using Vue's template syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct syntax to display the userCount value from the dashboardData object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metric card isn't displaying the user count correctly. Remember to use double curly braces {{ }} to output reactive data values in the template.

steps.title: Create revenue metric card
steps.instruction: Inside the template's metrics-section div, add a second metric card div that displays the formatted revenue from the reactive dashboardData state. Use the same structure as the user count card but with appropriate labels and values.
steps.hint: Add another div with class 'metric-card' inside the existing metrics-section. Display 'Revenue' as the label and format the revenue value with a dollar sign.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding another metric card

Revenue

${{ dashboardData.revenue }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will now display two metric cards: one for user count and one for revenue, both using reactive data from dashboardData.
successCriteria: A second metric card div is added to the metrics-section with proper labels and displays formatted revenue data from dashboardData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a metric card, but check that it displays the revenue value correctly formatted with a dollar sign.
steps.feedbackWrong: The revenue metric card wasn't added correctly. Make sure to add a div with class 'metric-card' inside the metrics-section that shows 'Revenue' and the formatted value.

steps.title: Create active users metric card
steps.instruction: Add a third metric card div inside the metrics-section that displays the activeUsers value from dashboardData.
steps.hint: Add another div with class 'metric-card' containing an h3 for the label and a paragraph to display dashboardData.activeUsers.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: another metric card

Active Users

{{ dashboardData.activeUsers }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes three metric cards, with the third displaying activeUsers from the reactive state.
successCriteria: A third metric card div with class 'metric-card' is added inside the metrics-section, containing an h3 with 'Active Users' and a paragraph showing {{ dashboardData.activeUsers }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a metric card, but check that it displays the activeUsers value correctly and has the proper structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The active users metric card is missing or incorrect. Ensure you add a div with class 'metric-card' containing an h3 and a paragraph that shows dashboardData.activeUsers.

steps.title: Add update button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template that triggers the updateMetrics function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to bind the click event to your updateMetrics function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler in Vue
<button @click="handleClick">Update Data</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the dashboard that will call the updateMetrics function when clicked.
successCriteria: The template contains a button element with @click="updateMetrics".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it's missing the click event binding. Make sure to use @click="updateMetrics" to wire it to your handler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly connected to the updateMetrics function. Check that you've added a button element with the @click directive pointing to updateMetrics.
